newsitem.title: UK: Eskom says privatisation plans on hold for 2-3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Eskom says privatisation plans on hold for 2-3 yrs.

text.p: South African electricity utility Eskom's privatisation plans were on hold for the next two to three years, executive director of finance Willem Kok said on Tuesday.
"Eskom's assets will not be privatised for the next two to three years," he said at the presentation of Eskom's annual results in London.
"The government has said that in the next two to three years they're going to look at other entities and not at Eskom, so for the medium term Eskom is off the table," Kok told Reuters.
He said the delay was due to "the current stance of management, the unions and the government".
Kok said "corporatisation" of Eskom would take place from mid-year when the utility would have to start paying tax and dividends, but with the government still as sole shareholder.
Eskom has recently moved into the limelight as South Africa's privatisation drive slowly gains momentum but plans to sell mothballed stations have been opposed by labour unions.
Concerns centre around job losses and the potential loss of state control in a vital sector of the economy.
Government, unions and Eskom have been trying to settle fundamental differences on the approach to restructuring the electricity giant in the Restructuring and Transformation Committee.
The privatisation programme has been slowed by opposition from trade unions which have now been guaranteed formal consultation on the sale of state assets.
